title: Triangular minimality for planar Coulomb renormalized energy
main_claim: Sandier–Serfaty conjecture: the covolume-one triangular lattice field minimizes the planar Coulomb renormalized energy W over A_1. Via Bétermin–Sandier this also gives the BHS linear term for spherical log energy. The proof has five steps: a lower bound on square tori via a glued Voronoi-sector trial potential H and the exact dual identity W_n(h)=Σ_S J(S)+½∫|∇(h−H)|²; an affine sector bound J(S) ≥ K+λA+μθ obtained from two scalar inequalities certified by interval arithmetic; the incidence count ≤6n; separation of minimizers at r*=1/√π; and transfer to the plane through Sandier–Serfaty periodic approximation.

issues.description: The scalar inequalities (2g_d(x) ≥ K for d ≥ b, and the negative part of G bounded by −K) rest entirely on the C++/Boost interval certificate, which could not be rerun here because Boost.Multiprecision is not installed. The negative-part margin is small, about 0.001 against −K ≈ 0.00348. The min of 2g−K is reached exactly at the stationary point and is handled by a Hessian-convexity argument on D_0, so correctness depends on the certificate. Independent floating-point spot checks agree with the claims.
issues.evidence: Python rebuild with 12 modes on a 1e6-point radial grid, d in [b, 0.75] plus large d, s in [0, 1.5]: min(2g−K) ≈ 2.6e-8 at (d,s) ≈ (p, x0); max ∫max(0,−G) = 0.002488 at d = b, below −K = 0.003482; f(l) = 0.00448 > 0; −πB(l)−λ/2 = 0.0774 > 0.

coverage: Read in full: the introduction, the reduction (Sec. 2), geometry and duality (Sec. 3), calibration (Sec. 4), the conclusion (Sec. 7), and the key parts of the tails (Sec. 5) and computation (Sec. 6: exterior signs, compact rectangle, Hessian/convexity step, soundness proposition). Checks made by hand: the dual identity's Green's-identity signs and counterterm; trace matching on edges and on vertex rays; the substitution s = d tanφ giving G = (d/t²)f − (s²/(dt²))e; the case analysis in the signed-endpoint lemma; the screened-potential minimum principle (−ΔΨ ≥ 2π/n on Ω, |Ω| < n); the Euler/degree count E ≤ 3n; that b < 1/(2√π); and that the hexagon mode cancellation gives H = h_△ − C_△. Independent numerics: (1) Ewald computation of πR_1 for the triangular torus, −4.15041280768, which matches the value implied by C_BHS exactly; (2) a from-scratch Python rebuild of the radial data b_m, U_m, u_m, B, D_i and of f0, e, λ, μ, K, giving λ = −6.73003 (paper: −6.731 < λ < −6.729) and 6K+λ+2πμ = −4.1504128071, so the calibration identity holds to 6e-10; (3) a grid check of both scalar inequalities and the exterior sign tests, all passed. Not done: rerunning the C++ certificate (Boost missing), and a detailed audit of the tail constants in Sec. 5, the mesh error bookkeeping, and Appendix 8.
sibling_notes: Family 090 siblings (rank 362 atomic certificate, rank 175 universal optimality) both reported no_gap_found. They concern Gaussian/universal optimality and share no lemmas with this Voronoi-sector Coulomb proof. All three use the same normalization for the triangular lattice.
